<reason>CON held the decisive distinction: screening, limits, monitoring and denial authority are safeguards, while therapeutic purpose is an extra use-ban. PRO showed brain-writing needs stringent control but never justified withholding a device after those controls are met, retreating to that any residual risk is never worth a nonmedical benefit. That zero-risk value judgment conceded CON's framing and left PRO's blanket medical-only rule undefended.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's screening-vs-exclusivity turn: license analogy shows eligibility checks can coexist with consumer access, and authority to reject unsafe users does not justify excluding safe nonmedical uses.</best_rebuttal>
